headline: Approved NGrid and Verizon pole request on Oakhurst Road; set Fall Town Meeting for Oct. 19.
summary: Officials reviewed draft fall Town Meeting warrant articles, including a $500,000 feasibility study for HVAC problems at the Early Learning Center and Elementary School. A proposed fire museum at Waters Farm was presented for information, with no town funds to be used. Residents also heard about the accessory dwelling unit article and a state duplex bill.
decisions: Approved the August 4, 2026 meeting minutes, 3-0 with one abstention.
Approved NGrid and Verizon pole hearing #31347368 for Oakhurst Road, 4-0.
Approved signing the Select Board Governance Framework, 4-0.
Approved holding the Fall Town Meeting on the 3rd Monday of October, Oct. 19, as the Bylaws require, 4-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Select person Limanek motions to accept as presented the August 4, 2026 Select Board meeting minutes as presented, Select Watkins seconds passes 3-0 and 1 abstention (Spengler abstains-absent from 8/4/26 meeting) - Limanek “aye”, Watkins “aye” Anderson “aye”

Select Watkins motions to approve Pole Hearing #31347368 from NGrid & Verizon for Oakhurst Road as advertised in the July 30, 2026 Millbury Sutton Chronicle Select Spengler seconds passes 4-0 with roll call vote: Limanek “aye”, Watkins “aye” Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”.

Sign the Select Board Governance Framework- hearing no discussion Select Spengler motions to sign the Select Board Governance Framework, Select Limanek seconds passes 4-0 with roll call vote. Limanek “aye”, Watkins “aye” Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”

Select Limanek motions to hold the Fall Town Meeting date required in the Bylaws to the 3rd Monday of October (Oct. 19th) Select Spengler seconds passes 4-0 with roll call - Limanek “aye”, Watkins “aye” Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”

                                                                                                    Meeting Minutes
                                                 Minutes Accepted and file with the Town Clerk   9/8/2026  with a roll call vote of    3-1   
   Ettamarna abstains/Limanek not present
                                                                                             6:00 p.m. –  August 18, 2026                  
   HYBRID MEETING Roll Call vote taken:
Members in Attendance:
Chairperson Anderson, Select members Limanek, Watkins & Spengler all present and in person (Vice Chair Ettamarna absent)
Also attending in person: Town Manager Austin Cyganiewicz & Deb Jacques, secretary
Public Forum –  Andrea Mattei- 21 Golf Ridge Drive attended the Planning Board meeting 8/17/26 and was here to speak on the ADU
warrant article. Andrea states it may have to be changed as to the unit count per lot. She does support the wording in its current form. 
Andrea states if the duplex bylaw passes we will have to amend this bylaw if it passes at Town Meeting. Andrea states maybe this 
article should be tabled at town meeting and see what the outcome of this Duplex bill will be- this law will affect every town in 
Massachusetts.
Select person Limanek motions to accept as presented the August 4, 2026 Select Board meeting minutes as presented, Select Watkins 
seconds passes 3-0 and 1 abstention (Spengler abstains-absent from 8/4/26 meeting) -  Limanek “aye”, Watkins “aye” Anderson “aye”
*Public Pole Hearing*   Oakhurst Road- Select Watkins reads in to record the notice as posted in the July 30, 2026 Millbury Sutton 
Chronicle. Present from NGrid is Fritze Jolin- design engineer. Fritze states this request is due to a drive way being installed. Select 
Limanek questions is it new construction or just moving the driveway. Fritze replies new construction. Hearing no further comments 
questions Select Watkins motions to close the Public Hearing Select Limanek seconds passes 4-0 with roll call vote Limanek “aye”, 
Watkins “aye” Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”. Select Watkins motions to approve Pole Hearing #31347368 from NGrid & Verizon 
for Oakhurst Road as advertised in the July 30, 2026 Millbury Sutton Chronicle Select Spengler seconds passes 4-0 with roll call vote: 
Limanek “aye”, Watkins “aye” Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”. 
Proposed Sutton Fire Museum at Waters Farm: present is Deputy Chief Robin Dresser. Town Manager Cyganiewicz states there is no 
action required by the Select Board- this is only informative. Dept. Chief Dresser addresses the Select Board – he presented this to 
Fire Chief Matt Belsito 6 months ago- Chief Belsito is in full support. Robin also met with Paul Schaefer and Waters Farm board 
members. Robin states this will be a long project- there will be fund raisers, donations volunteers. There will be no town funds used 
for this. Select Watkins questions if this will be under the Waters Farm purview, the town or the Fire Dept. Robin replies Waters farm 
or the Fire Dept. Select Limanek questions if this will be just Sutton Fire Dept. or other towns? Robin replies Sutton but there may be 
a few smaller pieces on display. This will be open during Waters Farm Days as well as private appts. and a few other times. It will be 
run strictly on volunteer hours. Select Limanek asks Town Manager Cyganiewicz- Waters Farm is Town owned- would this be 
required to fall under the procurement laws- Austin replies no- because no town funds will be used and if there will be any earmarks 
from the state the language will include the non-profit information. Select Spengler has no issues with this project as long as it is not 
funded by town funds. Dan also asks if all the items are currently stored in station 2- Robin replies they are stored in all 3 locations but
will definitely allow a little breathing room once the items are removed.  Paul Schaefer (present)Uxbridge Road- states Waters Farm 
board members were enthusiastic and fully support this.
Sign the Select Board Governance Framework- hearing no discussion Select Spengler motions to sign the Select Board Governance 
Framework, Select Limanek seconds passes 4-0 with roll call vote. Limanek “aye”, Watkins “aye” Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”
www.suttonma.gov
Review Draft Fall Town Meeting Warrant- Town Manager Cyganiewicz- Article 1 is budgetary, 2 is OPEB funding (free cash should 
be certified by Sept. 8th) this will give us the amount that will be appropriated into the OPEB expense acct., Artic. 3 is appropriation to
the SPED stabilization acct., #4 is previous year bills (currently at $1300.00). #5 is to raise & appropriate $153,000. out of the Sewer 
retained earnings for 2 vehicles, #6 is to replace a container and compaction container at the Trans. Station ($26,000.) #7 is to engage 
in a 3rd party consulting service for Personnel Classification & Wage system ($32,000.). #8 is to address the issue of the HVAC issues 
at the Early Learning Center (built in 1973) & the Elementary School (1999). Originally this was to be an MSBA project- after a walk 
thru- it would have required replacing the roof on the ELC which is in good condition as well as the project just completed that 
replaced the blocks holding the solar panels. The School has decided to not join with the MSBA. The School Committee has decided 
to go to the Alternate article- raise & appropriate $500,000. for an OPM, feasibility study & schematic design. This will go thru the 
proper bid process.  Select Watkins questions the square footage required per student, the declining enrollment and what will the town 
do if the voters turn this down at Town Meeting. Austin states we would have to move to an aggressive capital plan. Chair Anderson 
questions if the faulty HVAC is due to its age or lack of maintenance. Town Manager Cyganiewicz states the current administration is 
doing a great job trying to keep up with the HVAC needs. Select Limanek states it would be cheaper to maintain/repair the current 
infrastructure then build a new school. Present is School Committee Chair Chris Matera 10 Atitash Ave- Chris states class rooms have
to be maintained at 68 degrees- that is not happening. Select Watkins questions do we have other space available to move the kids 
dealing with room temperature issues- there is the library.  Art. #9 is the accessory Dwelling Unit- present is Community 
Development Director Jen Hager. Jen reviews the wording- after brief discussion they move to #10 which was withdrawn earlier 
today. Town Manager Cyganiewicz questions if the Select Board would like to keep the Town Meeting on Sept. 21st or move back to 
the original date in October. Select Limanek voices we should go back to the October date which is in the Bylaws. Select Limanek 
motions to hold the Fall Town Meeting date required in the Bylaws to the 3rd Monday of October (Oct. 19th) Select Spengler seconds 
passes 4-0 with roll call - Limanek “aye”, Watkins “aye” Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”
Town Manager Update:
 Municibid posting scheduled to begin 9/7 and run to 9/22. Proceeds will go into miscellaneous revenue.
 Sept. 1st State Primary- deadline to register to vote 8/22, vote by mail deadline 8/25 and early voting 8/22-8/28.
 The Library will hold 2 informational meetings on 9/1 3-5pm and 6-7:30pm for 5-year strategic planning
 Block walkway at Tricentennial Park complete
 Roof at Simonian ELC almost complete.
 The 1st Triboard meeting last week was held. All meeting material is on line.
Select Board Round Table
Select. Limanek reads the lengthy list of needs for the Sutton Food Pantry along with different locations to drop off donations. The 
Sutton Food pantry is run on only donations- no town funds. This is the 25th year anniv. Of 9/11- there will be a ceremony at the 
Dudley Gendron on 9/12 @ noon- with speakers. Following the ceremony will be the annual Chicken Barbecue with all proceeds 
going to NEEDS to train dogs to help Veterans.  
Select. Watkins informs the public on labor day there will be a Labor Day breakfast from 7am-10:30. On 8/19 there will be a meeting 
at 6pm- Sr Center- to discuss the options of what to do with Mill #2 and #3 in Manchaug village as well as restoring some of the 
natural areas. In regards to the duplex bill – one of our focuses was on Land Use- we were going to focus on Marion’s Camp and 
Shaw Farm but there are some other important land use things that should be in our purview and it is this multi family law that would 
allow duplexes on absolutely every single family residential lot in the state. 
                                       List of documents used for meeting
Pole Hearing request- Oakhurst Road, Sutton Fire Museum at Waters Farm, Governance Framework document, draft Fall Town 
Meeting Warrant 
Select person Limanek motions to adjourn, Select. Watkins seconds passes 4-0 – Limanek “aye” Watkins “aye” Spengler “aye” 
Anderson “aye”
Meeting adjourned   7:43 pm
